Subject: Intermittent p95 latency spikes from Model H4Z (production)

Hi Jordan,

We've been seeing intermittent p95 latency spikes across our customer-facing flows that correlate with requests routed to Model H4Z (v2027-03-31). The spikes started late Wednesday and reappeared this morning — our telemetry shows tail latency up to 2.8s from a baseline ~800ms for a subset of longer prompts (context > 2k tokens).

Attaching a short sample of error traces and the extracted p95 by hour for the last 48 hours. This is impacting conversion on our diagnostic flow; we estimate ~6% failed UX interactions during the spikes. Can you confirm whether this model variant had any config/quantization changes in the last deploy window? We have a demo scheduled for Monday and would like to understand mitigation options and whether you can temporarily route us to a fallback variant.

Thanks,

Thanks for flagging — quick summary of what I found after a rapid check of the deploy and runtime: 

- Deploy changes (2027-03-31): no model weight changes, but we shipped a new kernel prioritization tweak intended to reduce overhead for short-context fanout. That tweak can increase CPU contention in the scheduler for long-context requests under specific concurrency shapes.
- Serving telemetry: the affected buckets are requests with context length > 1800 tokens + realtime augmentation calls. Those are hitting the path where the new prioritization interacts poorly with our KV cache eviction timing; that causes repeated recomputation and transient tail increases.
- Fallback options: H4Z-v2027-02-10 (older kernel) is fully compatible but slightly higher cost; H4Z-quant-lite reduces memory pressure and has historically lower tail latency for long contexts.

Proposed short-term plan (for Jordan to share with DeltaCare):
1) Provisional carveout: route DeltaCare traffic to H4Z-quant-lite for next 72 hours. This requires a routing override (we can do per-account routing) and a formal carveout notice to procurement.
2) Rollback criteria / automatic reversion: if p95 exceeds 1.6s for > 20 minutes or error-rate delta > 2.5% for 10 minutes on the fallback, we will automatically revert traffic back to the original variant and open a high-priority investigation.
3) Mitigation work: engineering will revert the kernel prioritization in a staged patch (ETA 48 hours) and run a targeted canary against long-context workloads.
4) Acceptable carveout billing: route will be metered at standard hosted rates; propose a one-time technical credit (5%) for the inconvenience — Jordan can approve commercial terms.

I'll prepare the quick MAP doc with the above and attach it.

-Kim
Principal Reliability PM | Redwood Inference
kimberly.park@redwood.com

Attachment: provisional-carveout-MAP-v1.docx

Agree with Kimberly's assessment and the proposed thresholds. I authorize the provisional carveout with the following additions: 

- Authorization window: 72 hours starting as soon as DeltaCare confirms acceptance and we activate the routing override.
- Rollback automation: operations to implement the automatic reversion rules Kim specified. If the automatic reversion triggers, notify DeltaCare + internal on-call and do not re-route until post-mortem and a patch is applied.
- Commercial: approve a 5% one-time technical credit. Jordan, please coordinate commercial communication and confirm procurement acceptance.

Jordan — once you get DeltaCare's go-ahead, instruct ops to switch to H4Z-quant-lite and send a short MAP (attached) that documents the rollback triggers, duration, and contacts. I'll be on standby for any escalation.
